title: [Bugfix][ROCm][MLA] Normalize FlashAttention LSE layout in mixed decode/prefill scheduling
bodyExcerpt:
## Overview

Fix ROCm MLA chunked-prefill failures by normalizing the log-sum-exp
(LSE) tensor returned by upstream FlashAttention to vLLM's expected
`[num_heads, num_query_tokens]` layout.

Upstream FlashAttention on ROCm returns the LSE tensor as
`[num_query_tokens, num_heads]`. The newer per-request MLA chunk
accumulation path expects the opposite layout. This causes a shape mismatch
when a mixed decode/prefill batch contains a continued prefill.

The normalization is performed at the FlashAttention backend boundary so
the rest of the MLA implementation receives a consistent LSE layout.

## Claims

- Fixes MLA inference crashes on ROCm when chunked prefill produces
  per-request continuation chunks.
- Normalizes upstream FlashAttention LSE output from `[tokens, heads]` to
  vLLM's `[heads, tokens]` contract.
- Preserves the existing CUDA/XPU path, where vLLM FlashAttention already
  returns LSE in the expected layout.
- Does not affect the separate ROCm AITER FlashAttention backend.

## Validation

### Reproducer

The issue was reproduced with the following configuration:

| Setting | Value |
| --- | --- |
| Model | GLM-4.7-Flash (`Glm4MoeLiteForCausalLM`) |
| GPU | AMD Radeon Pro W7900 |
| vLLM | `0.29.1.dev0+g98dff2a81.d20261002.rocm101` |
| PyTorch | `2.13.0+rocm10.1.0` |
| HIP | `7.16.26385` |
| FlashAttention | `2.8.3` |
| Tensor parallel size | 2 |
| Maximum batched tokens | 2048 |
| Input/output length | 128/128 |
| Request concurrency | 64 |

title: [Perf][HiSparse] Fuse per-layer slot invalidation and shorten the all-resident resolver path
bodyExcerpt:
## Purpose

Cut HiSparse's per-layer decode overhead on the GPU and in launches:

- **One slot-invalidation launch per step.** Today it's one eager launch per leader layer after the forward graph (61 for DeepSeek-V3.2). The kernel now runs over (written tokens × index groups) using a cached device table of each group's `device_global_indices`. `HiSparseRuntime.invalidate_written_slots` is replaced by `HiSparseSlotInvalidator`.
- **Resolver masks CUDA-graph padding rows itself** from `num_valid_rows`. This removes the per-layer `copy_` + `masked_fill_` and the `request_ids`/`row_indices` buffers.
- **Cheaper all-resident resolver path.** Resident and invalid entries resolve before the host-row hash table is built, with an early exit when no host rows exist. Power-of-two block arithmetic uses shift/mask.

Stacked on #60083 (includes its commit); review only the top commit.

title: [HiSparse] Stage host-backed prefills into a reserved buffer
bodyExcerpt:
## Purpose

Fixes scenario 2 of #60420. When a prompt's KV has spilled to host (e.g. a 1M-token prompt on a HiSparse decoder), prefill copies its history into a GPU buffer one layer at a time. Startup never reserves that buffer, so a long prompt can OOM a running server.

- Stage into the shared workspace, reserved before profiling and sized for one `max_model_len` request (about 0.55 GiB at 1M tokens).
- Split prefill requests into groups that each fit, one staging plan per group. The four sparse MLA backends loop over the groups through `HiSparseMLAIndexGroup.staged_prefills`.

Two related fixes are split out so this one stays small: #60706 bounds two other staging temporaries, and #60707 removes the decode/prefill `torch.cat`.

The builder no longer replaces `prefill.block_table` with the staged block table; only the MHA prefill paths read it, and they're off under HiSparse.

title: [HiSparse] Own GPU residency instead of editing core block-table rows
bodyExcerpt:
## Purpose

Fixes #60109. This is an alternative to #60117 and #60123.

HiSparse stored GPU residency by editing core block-table rows after sending them: it adopted GPU copies of host prefix pages, and nulled pages the pool reused. The edits reached the worker through `SchedulerOutput.block_table_updates`, and #60109 was a new request's row arriving twice in one step. With this PR, HiSparse owns residency, and the worker only ever sees core rows grow (the scheduler fills an imported prefix's null tail entry before the row is first sent):

- **Scheduler:** `HiSparseResidentManager` records adopted and lost pages as per-request `residency_changes`. For each scheduled request, the coordinator sends the block ids of only the pages the worker lacks (new pages, plus pages adopted or lost since the last send; a new or re-admitted request gets its full row once), in HiSparse's connector metadata. At batch scale some request gains a page nearly every decode step.
- **Worker:** HiSparse keeps one persistent device table `[request state rows, resident groups, pages]`, written with one scatter per step that carries updates. It adds to core's per-group resident block tables, which still drive KV writes; HiSparse reads residency from its own table. The decode resolver kernel indexes it by state row, so nothing is copied per step; prefill staging gathers its rows once per batch.
- **Core:** `block_table_updates` is removed and `update_requests` is back to its pre-HiSparse form. `add_requests` is unchanged.

**Why this over #60117/#60123:** those keep HiSparse's row edits in core (in `update_requests`, and in `add_requests` for #60123). This removes them entirely. Cost: about 230 added lines versus about 10, plus one int32 table: about 18 MB at 256 seqs × 18k context × 61 groups, and about 0.25 GB at 512 seqs × 128k. It is allocated after memory profiling, like MRv2's block tables.

title: [Perf][Core][Mamba] Export prefill checkpoints at or before the initial-state column
bodyExcerpt:
## Overview

With a fine-grained prefix match unit (e.g. `--prefix-match-unit 128` on GLM-5.3-Flash, KDA linear attention + sparse MLA), many partial-hit prefills pay one extra fixed-cost prefill step. The scheduler rejects the in-pass prefill checkpoint whenever its column is at or before the column holding the initial state, then splits the prefill at the checkpoint boundary. This PR lets a request's first chunk export that checkpoint in the same pass, so those prefills run as a single step. It also fixes a related cache-publishing bug in `MambaManager`. Follow-up to #56960; related to #59146, #59175, #59759 and #58021.

## Claims

- Partial-hit prefills whose checkpoint column is at or before the initial-state column (`checkpoint_col <= (start - 1) // block_size`) no longer split at the tail boundary. On GLM-5.3-Flash TP8 with pmu128, a hit of 2944/3300 tokens now prefills in one step. Median TTFT at c=1 goes from 58.8 ms to 41.4 ms. At c=16 it goes from 404 ms to 286 ms.
- No accuracy change: GSM8K and a multi-turn GSM8K that feeds the model's own answers back (every turn after the first is a prefix hit) match the unpatched image and the baseline. Prefix hit rates are unchanged.
- Fix: when a chunk resumed mid-block and ran past the block boundary, `MambaManager.cache_blocks` published that slot under its full-block hash, although the slot holds the initial (or checkpoint) state. A later request could then match it.

## Validation

GLM-5.3-Flash on 8xH100. Settings: TP8, `FLASHMLA_SPARSE`, `fp8_ds_mla`, `--max-num-batched-tokens 8192`, prefix caching on, `--prefix-match-unit 128`. title: [Bugfix][MoE] Decouple DeepEP low-latency dispatch size from max_num_batched_tokens
bodyExcerpt:
## Overview

`--all2all-backend deepep_low_latency` crashes at startup whenever `--max-num-batched-tokens` is set above a few hundred. This happens with an ordinary prefill-friendly config such as `--max-num-batched-tokens 4096`. The cause is that the per-rank dispatch capacity of the DeepEP LL buffers is taken directly from `max_num_batched_tokens`. This PR decouples the two: the LL buffers are sized for a fixed number of tokens per rank, and larger forward passes are split into several dispatch rounds that stay in sync across the DP ranks.

Related: #57894 / #57915 (draft). That PR adds a fail-fast error for the same 32 GiB limit, but the config still cannot run. This PR makes the config run.

## Claims

- DP8xEP8 `deepep_low_latency` with `--max-num-batched-tokens 4096` now starts and serves correctly with no `NVSHMEM_*` env tuning. Before this PR it crashed in `deep_ep.Buffer.__init__`.
- The memory used by the LL RDMA buffer and the batched-expert workspaces no longer grows with `max_num_batched_tokens`.
- A clear `ValueError` is raised when a user-set `NVSHMEM_QP_DEPTH` is too small. Previously this was a bare `AssertionError` deep inside DeepEP.
- No behavior change for the default LL config: when `max_num_batched_tokens` is not set it already defaults to 256, so no chunking happens and the buffer size is unchanged.
- No behavior change for other all2all backends. Chunking only triggers when a rank's batch exceeds `prepare_finalize.max_num_tokens_per_rank()`. Other prepare/finalize implementations report `max_num_batched_tokens` or `None` there, so they never trigger it.

## Validation

title: [Bugfix][Attention] Re-plan DSA indexer decode schedule for DBO's reduced DeepGEMM SM count
bodyExcerpt:
## Overview

With `--enable-dbo` and an all2all backend that reserves communication SMs (e.g. DeepEP high-throughput), DSA models (DeepSeek-V3.2, GLM-5.x) crash in the sparse-attention indexer as soon as a microbatched step contains a decode-branch request:

```
RuntimeError: Assertion error (csrc/apis/attention.hpp:346): _schedule_meta_size == num_sms + 1 and _meta_info_size == 2
```

The indexer builder plans DeepGEMM's paged-MQA-logits schedule for the whole GPU, but DBO lowers DeepGEMM's SM count (`set_num_sms(total - VLLM_DBO_COMM_SMS)`) while the microbatches run. This PR re-plans the schedule at the call site when the two counts differ. No existing issue or PR covers this (searched `schedule_meta_size`, `dbo indexer num_sms`, `paged_mqa_logits set_num_sms`: 0 results). Rechecked 2026-10-08 against open PRs: #56476 (DeepSeek-V4.1 per-microbatch index state) also edits `sparse_attn_indexer.py`, in different lines, and does not touch the schedule metadata.

## Claims

- Fixes the DSA indexer decode crash under DBO (Model Runner V1 and V2, CUDA + DeepGEMM).
- The re-planned schedule gives bit-identical indexer logits, so the fix does not change results: with it, GLM-5.3 accuracy under DBO matches DBO with SM partitioning disabled (`VLLM_DBO_COMM_SMS=0`), where this code path never runs.
- Separately, GLM-5.3 accuracy with DBO on is well below DBO off (GSM8K ~0.6 vs 0.93) with or without this change. That is a separate, pre-existing DBO bug in GLM-5.x's shared top-k layers that this crash was hiding, fixed in #60734 (see Validation).
- No cost when the SM count is unchanged (one host-side `get_num_sms()` per indexer layer). Under DBO, one ~9 µs metadata kernel per microbatch per forward, reused by all indexer layers. No host syncs; CUDA-graph safe.
- XPU / ROCm paths unchanged.

## Validation

This branch is rebased onto main @ 240785b8; the rebase did not change the patch (same `git patch-id`). The unit and related tests below were re-run on the rebased commit

title: [Bugfix][HiSparse] Carry adopted prefix pages in the new request's row
bodyExcerpt:
## Purpose

Fixes #60109: HiSparse servers crash with an illegal memory access when a new request hits a prefix whose published host pages still have GPU copies.

The coordinator adopts those copies after the scheduler has already built the request's `NewRequestData`, so the adopted row went out as a `block_table_updates` entry. For a new request, model runner V2 then stages two full-row writes for the same row in one step (`add_requests`, then `update_requests`), and the staged-write kernel applies them in parallel with no ordering. A rank that kept the pre-adoption row saw null resident pages, while the scheduler reported every context page resident. The resident-prefill shortcut then sent the prefill rows through the decode residency resolver, whose host union overflowed `max_union_rows` and faulted.

The fix puts the adopted row in the new request's `block_ids`; `block_table_updates` stays for running requests. HiSparse-only (`hisparse/connector.py`).

Note: MRv2's staged block-table writer doesn't order overlapping writes to the same row. This PR stops HiSparse from producing them; changing that in core is a separate discussion.

title: [Bugfix][MRV2] Write a new request's block-table update once
bodyExcerpt:
## Purpose

Fixes #60109 (HiSparse servers crash with an illegal memory access on prefix hits).

A `block_table_updates` row supersedes a request's normal block-table write, and `update_requests` already skips `new_block_ids` for running requests that have one. New requests lacked that guard. `add_requests` staged the `NewRequestData` row, `update_requests` staged the update, both for the same row in the same step, and `_apply_write_kernel` applies staged writes as unordered programs. Ranks could keep either row. With HiSparse prefix-copy adoption, ranks that kept the stale row read null resident pages, and the decode residency resolver overflowed.

Fix: `add_requests` skips the `NewRequestData` row when a table update exists, and `update_requests` writes the update as before.

## Why this instead of #60117

- **It fixes the race where it happens.** MRv2 accepts two unordered writes to one row; #60117 only stops today's single producer (HiSparse) from sending them.
- **It's smaller and symmetric.** Five lines extend the guard `update_requests` already has. #60117 instead has the HiSparse connector rewrite an already-built `NewRequestData`, which also changes what every other reader of that field sees.
- **It costs nothing for other users.** A dict lookup per new request, and one fewer GPU row write when an update exists.

title: [RFC]: A standard for MonoKernels in vllm/models
bodyExcerpt:
### Motivation.

A **MonoKernel** is a persistent kernel that runs most or all of one decoder layer's decode step in a single launch. This RFC proposes one way to add them under `vllm/models/<model>/<vendor>/`:

- The layer loop calls `mono.forward_layer(...)`, which launches the layer's kernel or calls the vLLM layer unchanged. The module tree and parameter names never change.
- A shared library, `vllm/models/common/mono/` (~650 lines), owns what every MonoKernel repeats: refusals, routing, fail-stop, health words, peer memory, cache re-binding.
- A model adds its kernel plus ~400 lines, instead of a 6–24k-line stack of its own.

The standard starts ROCm-only, where all known MonoKernels live (GLM-5.2, DeepSeek-V4.1, MiniMax-M3, Kimi-K3). CUDA joins with a CUDA co-author.

#### Why MonoKernels

At low concurrency, decode is bound by launch overhead and weight reads, and a MonoKernel removes most of both. On 8× MI350X a graph-mode GLM-5.2 decode step issues ~2,459 kernels in vLLM. With the MonoKernel it issues ~210: 75 MonoKernel launches plus ~135 for dense layers 0–2, input prep and the head.

title: [Bugfix][KV Connector][ROCm] MoRIIO: support kernel-block-split 4-D K…
bodyExcerpt:
## Summary

On a GLM-5.3-Flash 1P/1D MoRIIO READ deployment, registering the sparse-indexer ("kpool") KV cache aborts with `Unsupported MoRIIO MLA cache shape for layer …self_attn.indexer`. For an `MLAAttentionSpec` carrying a `storage_block_size`, `create_kv_cache_views` hands connectors a **kernel-block-split** 4-D view whose leading dim counts kernel blocks, not manager blocks (`r = block_size / storage_block_size`; `r = 17` at EP8/TP1). MoRIIO's standardized 4-D branch only accepted `r == 1`, so it rejected the indexer view. Block ids on the wire are always manager ids, so geometry must be expressed in manager blocks.

**This PR teaches `get_layer_transfer_geometry` (`moriio_layout.py`) to read kernel-split views in manager blocks:**
- Accept `spec.num_states % N == 0`, derive `r = num_states // N`, and report `num_blocks = B/r`, `block_stride = stride[0]*r`, `block_len = num_states*slot_size`.
- Reject any view that isn't `r` dense, contiguous kernel pages per block, so a malformed layout errors instead of silently transferring wrong bytes.

Bit-identical for `r == 1` (e.g. DeepSeek MLA); no wire-format or metadata change. ~20 lines in one file. (This supersedes the fork's kernel-unit approach — deriving `r` from the view and spec removes the `kbpb`/`layer_num_blocks` protocol additions, since `r` is a per-layer property identical on both legs.)

title: [Bugfix] Gate the FA4 masked-MHA sparse prefill on prefill-query quantization, not KV cache dtype
bodyExcerpt:
## Description

`_is_masked_mha_available` rejects the FA4 masked-MHA sparse prefill whenever the KV cache is quantized: `fa_version == 4 and not is_quantized_kv_cache(kv_cache_dtype)`. That conflates the KV cache dtype with the prefill query dtype. The masked path never reads FP8 KV as FP8: context rows go through the same `gather_and_maybe_dequant_cache` the dense path already uses, and the suffix K/V are the current step's bf16 projections. An FP8 prefill query is what the kernel cannot consume, and for NoPE-dims models like GLM-5.3-Flash it is unreachable anyway: no prefill backend supports the `(256, 0, 256)` dims for prefill query quantization, so the query is always bf16. As the gate stood, every prefill token past 2048 context rode per-token sparse MQA with topk random KV gathers, inside the regime where the measured threshold table already routes masked MHA ahead of MQA.

This gates on the actual prefill-query quantization state instead. `fp8_ds_mla` / `nvfp4_ds_mla` and the other packed byte formats stay excluded via an explicit dtype allow-list, the HiSparse routing is untouched, and with no config present the gate stays conservative-off for quantized dtypes, preserving current behavior.

| config | before | after |
|---|---|---|
| GLM-5.3-Flash: fp8 KV, FA4, prefill q bf16 | masked-MHA vetoed, per-token sparse MQA for all prefill past 2048 ctx | masked-MHA eligible |
| fp8 KV, prefill query quantization on + backend supports it | vetoed | vetoed (unchanged) |
| fp8_ds_mla / nvfp4_ds_mla / e5m2 / per-token-head / nvfp4 KV | vetoed | vetoed (dtype allow-list) |
| auto / f16 / bf16 KV | unchanged | unchanged |
| fa3 / non-SM100 | unavailable | unavailable |

Draft until the unlocked path is run end-to-end with an FP8 KV cache; the table above is code-verified but not yet executed.

title: [Bugfix] Size the HiSparse hot buffer from the rounded sparse top-k width
bodyExcerpt:
## Description

HiSparse sizes the per-request hot buffer twice, from two different values. The scheduler builds `ResolvedHiSparseConfig` from `hf_config.index_topk`; the model allocates the top-k buffer at `round_up(index_topk + kpool - 1, 128)` wide and derives `region_stride` from that width. For any `index_kpool > 1` model the stride is strictly larger than the scheduler-sized table, so the CUDA resolver's `hot_block_table` column check fails at the first host-backed decode ("hot_block_table has too few columns"), and with a larger explicit `device_buffer_size` the hot set silently mispredicts rows instead. Existing A/Bs never hit it because the validated models are kpool == 1.

This makes both sides read one shared `get_sparse_topk_buffer_width()` and asserts `blocks_per_request * block_size == region_stride` in `HiSparseConnectorWorker.register_kv_caches`, so a future mismatch fails at startup instead of mid-decode. DeepSeek-style kpool == 1 configs resolve to exactly `index_topk` and keep their sizing.

| model | scheduler rows (before) | worker rows | before | after |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| GLM-5.3-Flash (topk 2048, kpool 4) | 9 * 2048 = 18432 | 9 * round_up(2047, 128) = 19584 | column check fails / hot set off by 1152 rows | 19584 == 19584, boots clean |
| DeepSeek-style (kpool 1) | 9 * 2048 | 9 * 2048 | unchanged | unchanged |

Verified at block sizes 32/64/128 with the GLM-5.3-Flash MTP k=7 shape (19584 == 306 * 64).

title: [Perf] Shard the GLM kpool decode indexer across the attention TP group
bodyExcerpt:
## Description

`wq_b` is `ReplicatedLinear` and `wk` runs with TP disabled, so the GLM kpool decode scorer's inputs are bit-identical on every attention-TP rank: the paged MQA logits GEMM, the top-k, and the pool expand all run `tp_size` times per sparse layer per step, about 12 times per engine step with k=7 drafting.

This adds an opt-in row sharding behind `VLLM_GLM_KPOOL_DECODE_INDEXER_ROW_SHARD`. Rank `r` scores only requests `r::tp_size` via an `index_select` gather, builds the per-rank DeepGEMM schedule in-op, and the expanded pool ids (int32, about 2051 per row) are all-gathered and reordered locally. K-cache and tail-cache writes stay replicated, so outputs are unchanged. Every gate is host-side metadata identical on every rank, so CUDA-graph capture/replay and rank consistency hold. Verify batches at 32 or fewer requests keep the replicated path: the all-gather costs more than the GEMM it saves at that size.

title: [Perf] Prefer DeepSelect over persistent_topk for large indexer top-k batches on SM100/SM103
bodyExcerpt:
## Description

The sparse indexer decode top-k auto chain is `cooperative -> persistent -> per_row`. `cooperative_topk` applies only within `AUTO_COOPERATIVE_MAX_ROWS`, so anything larger goes to `persistent_topk`. For GLM-5.3-Flash with MTP k=7 at 32 seqs that is every verify batch: 256 rows, all on `persistent_topk`, which bins logits into a coarse histogram and can silently drop true top-k candidates when a trained indexer clusters its scores in one bin (#51782). The vendored DeepSelect extension handles exactly these shapes on the SM100/SM103 family and measured 191 us vs 616 us at 256 rows / 1M KV when it landed (#56464), but it stayed opt-in only.

This adds a `deep_select` branch in `_resolve_auto` between cooperative and persistent. The existing support checks (`_has_deep_select`, `_HAS_DEEP_SELECT_C`, `is_deep_select_supported`) stay, so other devices and unsupported strides/dtypes fall through to `persistent_topk` unchanged.

Measured on GLM-5.3-Flash (NVFP4), 8x B300 (SM103), TP8, FP8 KV cache, MTP k=7, 1M context, `vllm bench serve`, random dataset, seed 42, medians of 3 warm runs:

| workload (1024-in / 1024-out) | TPOT mean | TPOT p99 | TTFT median |
|---|---|---|---|
| 8 concurrent | 5.40 -> 5.05 ms (-6.5%) | 8.26 -> 7.05 ms (-14.6%) | 288 -> 341 ms |
| 32 concurrent | 7.85 -> 6.89 ms (-12.2%) | 12.24 -> 12.84 ms | 1113 -> 1073 ms |
| 128K prompt, 64 out | 8.24 -> 6.82 ms (-17.2%) | 8.24 -> 6.82 ms | 502 -> 477 ms |

These are medians of 3 warm passes within one boot per arm; across reboots of the unpatched build, c8 and c32 TPOT varied by roughly 25% and 12% on this setup, so the smaller deltas are directional and the workload-level trend is the signal. title: [RFC]: Strcutured Outputs Not Respected When Reasoning Implicitly Ends
bodyExcerpt:
### Motivation.

I want to start a discussion on how implicit reasoning end can break structured ouptuts + spec decode.

### Background

For structured outputs, we only apply constrained decoding after reasoning ends. This is to allow models to reason while constraining the user-visible content.

At each decode step, the scheduler roughly calls:
1. `StructuredOutputManager.validate_tokens` to validate the draft tokens need constraining and trim any grammar-invalid tokens
2. `StructuredOutputManager.grammar_bitmask` to create bitmasks for the draft tokens that need constraining
3. `StructuredOutputManager.accpet_tokens` to advance grammar FSM over the constrained tokens

These three methods rely on a `StructuredOutputManager._get_constraint_start` helper to identify when reasoning ends. It returns `reasoning_end_index + 1`

### Implicit Reasoning Ends

Reasoning end is usually marked by a special token (e.g. `</think>` for GLM 5.3). However, reasoning can also end implicitly when the model starts emitting content or tool call without closing reasoning first (e.g. `<think> ... <tool_call>` instead of `<think> ... </think><tool_call>`). This presents challenges for strcutured output constraint start detection.

### Issues with Implicit Reasoning Ends

Currently, `StructuredOutputManager._get_constraint_start` assumes all reasoning end markers are explicit. For example, given `prefix <tool_call> suffix`,
1. `StructuredOutputManager.validate_tokens` doesn't validate the `<tool_call>`
2. `StructuredOutputManager.grammar_bitmask` creates bitmasks for `suffix` only
3. `StructuredOutputManager.accpet_tokens` advances grammar FSM over accepted `suffix` + bonux token only.

This leads to two issues:
- I1: `<tool_call>` may not be grammar valid, yet it is unconditionally accepted
- I2: if a model is required to make a tool call, it will be forced to generate duplicate `<tool_call>` because the grammar isn't aware of the first one #59608

Adds an `mxfp4_mla` KV cache dtype for the ROCm AITER sparse MLA backend on rope-free (NoPE) latents such as GLM-5.3-Flash. ## Overview

At DeepSeek-V4.1's 1M `max_model_len` on SM90, the indexer K-gather and FlashMLA prefill-gather reservations share a 5.16 GiB workspace per GPU. title: [KV Offload] Split the CPU offload region across shm files
bodyExcerpt:
Pre-faulting the CPU offload region is capped by its single `/dev/shm` file: page-cache inserts into one shmem file are serialized, so more workers or threads stop helping. On one H200 node, eight processes pre-faulting disjoint parts of a 64 GiB file reach 9.8 GiB/s in total. Given one file each, they reach 24.6 GiB/s, and sixteen files reach 44.8 GiB/s. #59430 hits the same ceiling with threads.

Split the region's rows over up to 32 files of at least 1 GiB each. The files are mapped back to back over one anonymous reservation, so the region stays contiguous. Workers with per-rank slots start pre-faulting on different files. Regions under 2 GiB, and other users of `SharedOffloadRegion`, keep a single file.

## Tests

4× H200, measured on `16d4ac4ba3` with this change (the touched files are unchanged on current main):

- GLM-5.3 W4A8, TP4 + EP, 256 GiB native CPU offload: the offload startup step fell from 63.6 to 38.3 s, and pre-faulting from 42.8 to 19.4 s. A 20k-token retrieval prompt answered 8/8 lookups cold and 8/8 after `/reset_prefix_cache`, with 3.9 GB reloaded from CPU.

title: [KV Offload] Give each rank its own CPU region outside the replicated layout
bodyExcerpt:
Outside the replicated layout, ranks never read each other's slots, but they still share one region whose rows interleave all ranks. Every rank pre-faults and pins its strided slots in the same shm file, contending with the others.

title: [Bugfix][MoE] Keep DeepEP high-throughput buffers alive across DBO streams
bodyExcerpt:
## Overview

Under DBO, `DeepEPHTPrepareAndFinalize` has DeepEP allocate its dispatch outputs on the DBO comm stream, then reads them on the compute stream; the combine input crosses the other way. The caching allocator is never told about these cross-stream reads, so the other microbatch's next DeepEP call can reuse a block and overwrite it before it is read. With the DeepGEMM FP8 MoE this crashes the engine at startup with an illegal memory access in `ep_scatter`. This PR calls `record_stream` on every tensor that crosses between the two streams.

A GitHub search found no existing issue or PR for this. Related: #46990 added a ROCm-only host sync after HT dispatch/combine under DBO, possibly for the same hazard (see Details). #27666 and #38451 fixed other DBO + DeepEP HT problems.

## Claims

- Fixes the startup crash with DBO + DeepEP high-throughput + the DeepGEMM FP8 MoE (`VLLM_USE_DEEP_GEMM=1 VLLM_MOE_USE_DEEP_GEMM=1`, the defaults). For GLM-5.3 FP8 on main, 2 of 2 runs crashed in the first microbatched step without the fix. On 0.29.0, so did all 7 runs that had neither the fix nor a serializing workaround (`CUDA_LAUNCH_BLOCKING`, no caching allocator, host sync). With the fix, full GSM8K scores 0.927 with CUTLASS linears and 0.912 with DeepGEMM linears (DBO off: 0.923).
- Covers both directions for every experts backend behind DeepEP HT: DeepEP's outputs (comm stream to compute stream) and the reduced expert output passed to combine (compute stream to comm stream; defensive on main, see Details). With `--enable-dbo`, GLM-5.x (DSA with shared top-k layers, `index_topk_freq > 1`) loses about a third of its GSM8K accuracy: 0.93 with DBO off, 0.61 with DBO on. title: [Bug]: HiSparse prefill can OOM a running server (unreserved host-history staging)

### Your current environment

vLLM main @ ad0f67a7ec, 1×B200, FlashInfer sparse MLA, fp8 KV, Model Runner V2.

### 🐛 Describe the bug

With HiSparse, a prompt that the server accepted can crash EngineCore with CUDA OOM, and running requests die with it. Two allocations in the HiSparse sparse-MLA prefill path aren't reserved by startup memory profiling. The profiling dummy run is one chunk of short pure prefills.

- **Full-history copy.** `stage_prefill_rows` → `HiSparseRuntime.gather_prefill_cache` copies the prefilling request's entire history from host into a temporary GPU buffer, one layer at a time: `(cdiv(seq_len, block_size), block_size, row_bytes)`, about 0.55 GiB at 1M tokens with 576 B rows. It is freed before the next layer, so it never holds the whole KV, but it grows with prompt length and nothing reserves it.
- **Decode/prefill output join.** In mixed batches, decode and prefill run as two kernels joined by `torch.cat`, about 1 GiB at 16K batched tokens.

There are two scenarios:

1. **Prompt fits on GPU, batched with decodes** (common aggregated serving). The copy and the join are both unnecessary here, because every page is GPU-resident. They run only because of the `num_decode_tokens == 0 and all_context_pages_resident` condition in `flashinfer_mla_sparse.py`. FlashAttn and FlashInfer SM120 have the same condition, and FlashMLA sparse BF16 copies on every prefill. Fixed by #60417.
2. **Prompt spilled to host**, e.g. a 1M-token prompt reaching a HiSparse decoder whose GPU can't hold its KV. The copy is required here, and its buffer is still not reserved. Fixed by #60424, which reserves a staging buffer at startup, sized for `max_model_len`.

title: [HiSparse] Read resident KV directly for mixed and BF16 prefills
bodyExcerpt:
## Purpose

Fixes scenario 1 of #60420. With HiSparse, a prefill batched with decodes copies its whole history from host and joins the decode and prefill outputs with `torch.cat`, even when all of its KV is on GPU. Startup doesn't reserve memory for either, so a long prompt can OOM a running server.

Now, when all KV is on GPU, all rows run in one kernel against the GPU pages. This covers FlashInfer, FlashAttn, FlashInfer SM120 and FlashMLA BF16 sparse MLA (#60419 folded in).

**Depends on a fix for #60109** (#60117, #60123 or #60647). In that race a new request's adopted prefix pages can stay null in the worker's resident block table. On main the decode and staging paths treat a null entry as a host read, so the race is harmless there. This PR's one-kernel path trusts the resident table, so it reads block 0 instead.

## Repro on main (ad0f67a7ec, 1×B200)

```bash
vllm serve <GLM-5.3-NVFP4> --load-format dummy --hf-overrides '{"num_hidden_layers": 4}' \
  --kv-cache-dtype fp8 --block-size 64 --max-model-len 1048576 --gpu-memory-utilization 0.97 \
  --scheduler-reserve-full-isl \
  --kv-transfer-config '{"kv_connector":"HiSparseConnector","kv_role":"kv_both","kv_connector_extra_config":{"host_pool_gib":24}}'
```

With 2 requests decoding, send a 1.04M-token prompt. EngineCore crashes at 934K context with `torch.OutOfMemoryError` in `torch.cat((decode_out, prefill_out))`. Without HiSparse, or with no concurrent decodes, it survives.

## Test Plan / Result

Same repro on 1×B200 (cut-down model: 4 layers, dummy weights), main vs this PR. Peak is the highest per-step memory above the step's starting allocation:

| Path | main | this PR | no HiSparse |
|---|---|---|---|
| FlashInfer, fp8 KV, util 0.97 | OOM at 934K (`torch.cat`); peak 6.30 GiB | OK, 58.6 s; peak 4.91 GiB | OK, 53.7 s; peak 4.91 GiB |
| FlashMLA BF16 (`--kv-cache-dtype bfloat16`), util 0.95 | OK, 184 s; peak 6.58 GiB | OK, 56.0 s; peak 4.48 GiB | OK, 55.2 s; peak 4.48 GiB |

## Overview

Structured output skipped a reasoning-end token that is also content, such as GLM's `<tool_call>` with no `</think>` before it. The grammar then forced a second `<tool_call>`, and `required`/named tool calls were lost. This PR feeds that token to the grammar, which matches what `extract_content_ids` already does. title: [Attention] Fetch MLA prefill workspace at use instead of init
bodyExcerpt:
## Purpose

The TRTLLM-ragged and FlashInfer MLA prefill backends keep a view of the shared workspace from `__init__`. When a later user, such as the sparse indexer's profile, grows the workspace, that view keeps the old buffer alive as an orphan. On GLM-5.3 on B200 that's 394 MB of GPU memory nobody uses.

Both backends now reserve their size at init without keeping a view, and fetch it in `prepare_metadata`, once per step. FlashInfer rebuilds its wrappers if the workspace has moved. The builder runs outside the DBO micro-batch threads, so both still use the micro-batch 0 slot, as on main.

Sharing the workspace is safe: TRTLLM ragged runs with multi-CTA KV off and uses it only for per-launch softmax stats, and FlashInfer cutlass prefill never touches it (it has its own 32 MB buffer).

## Test Result

Memory: 1×B200, GLM-5.3-NVFP4 cut to 4 layers with dummy weights, fp8 KV, `--max-model-len 1048576`, TRTLLM-ragged prefill:

| Available KV cache | 138.64 GiB | 139.02 GiB |
| GPU KV blocks | 861,476 | 863,866 |
| Orphaned 0.38 GiB block from `trtllm_ragged.py` `__init__` | present | gone |

title: [Model] Apply Transformers checkpoint renamings during weight loading
bodyExcerpt:
## Overview

Apply the weight renamings Transformers uses for each checkpoint (`transformers.conversion_mapping`) during weight loading, and update models so they no longer hand-map legacy checkpoint names. Supersedes #60131: GLM-5.3-Flash now uses the Transformers module names, so PEFT adapters trained with Transformers resolve without special-casing.

## Claims

- `get_checkpoint_renaming_mapper` builds the Transformers model on the meta device and takes the `WeightRenaming`s from `get_model_conversion_mapping`, so sub-model renamings are scoped exactly as in Transformers. `WeightConverter`s are skipped because vLLM fuses weights itself.
  - Renamings depend only on the `model_type`, even for custom code configs, because vLLM runs its own implementation either way.
  - vLLM's own config classes are converted to the native Transformers config class first. If the model still can't be built, the unscoped renamings of the `model_type` are used.
  - Regex quantization targets (`re:...`) are rewritten with the same renamings (`WeightsMapper.map_regex`), so e.g. Laguna NVFP4's `re:.*shared_expert\.(...)$` still matches the renamed `shared_experts`.
- The renamings are applied once, to the checkpoint weights, in `DefaultModelLoader` and `RunaiModelStreamerLoader`, so `hf_to_vllm_mapper` only has to map from current Transformers names.
  - LoRA, quantization configs and the `--mm-encoder-only` shard filter use the renamings followed by the model's mapper.
  - Drafts loaded from the target's checkpoint (MTP, DSpark) use the target's renamings.
  - The Transformers modeling backend no longer collects the renamings itself.
- Model updates. Every registered example checkpoint whose names Transformers renames was checked: ~80 architectures, ~70 of them native vLLM models.
  - **Renamed to the Transformers names:**
    - Mixtral, MiniMax-M2, MiniMax-M3, PhiMoE: `block_sparse_moe` -> `mlp`
    - Laguna: `shared_expert` -> `shared_experts`, gate bias
    - DeepSeek-V4: all backend

title: [Bugfix][HiSparse] Drop the unaccounted, write-only prefill mirror staging buffer
bodyExcerpt:
## Purpose

`initialize_hisparse_runtime_buffers` allocates a per-layer prefill mirror staging buffer (`num_layers × max_num_batched_tokens × row_bytes`) after the KV cache is sized, so memory profiling never counts it. That's about 0.69 GiB per GPU for GLM-5.3 (78 layers).

Nothing reads it: `HiSparseConnectorWorker.start_step` sets `mirror_from_resident = True` every step, so the host mirror always copies from the resident cache, and only dummy batches ever wrote the buffer. This PR removes it, along with `mirror_write_target` and `mirror_from_resident`.

Related: #60420.

this is a focused follow-up from our Shared-DCP work in #50009.

publish O/LSE -> signal -> one CTA per head

title: [Bugfix] Warm GLM DeepGEMM mHC pre-norm specializations
bodyExcerpt:
## Overview

GLM-5.3-Flash can finish startup and still pause to compile an mHC kernel when a new prompt length arrives. This PR moves those missing compilations to startup without changing the kernel math or split-K heuristic.

Addresses #60536. Depends on https://github.com/vllm-project/DeepGEMM/pull/29 for the compile-only entry point used by this implementation.

## Claims

- Register every reachable DeepGEMM mHC pre-norm specialization for GLM's configured token range, deduplicated by `(N, K, num_splits)`.
- Compile them through the existing startup warmup registry, without allocating input tensors or launching dummy kernels.
- Keep runtime split selection, kernel math, and backend selection unchanged.

## Details

### Why startup misses these kernels

The mHC pre-norm path contains a matrix multiplication implemented by DeepGEMM. It selects a split-K count (how many pieces to divide the reduction into) based on the number of tokens in the current engine step. Each distinct split count requires a separately compiled kernel. The row count `M` itself is dynamic, so there is no need to compile once per prompt length.

The existing selection is:

```python
num_splits = max(1, min(num_sms // ceil(M / 64), ceil(K / 64) // 4))
```

Here `M` is the step's token count, `K` is the input width, and `N` is the output width. For example, with 78 SMs and `K=16384`, `M=64`, `192`, and `16384` select 64, 26, and 1 splits respectively. Compiling the first and last does not compile the middle one. The number of required specializations depends on the GPU and configured token range; the issue's count of missing variants is not a universal constant.

The startup profile run and CUDA-graph capture exercise only some split counts. GLM does not register the remaining DeepGEMM variants for explicit warmup. title: [Performance][NIXL] BLHNC MLA caches lost whole-row registration in #53781 and now need more NIXL descriptors than LBHNC
bodyExcerpt:
## Your current environment
- GLM-5.3 (78 MLA + 21 indexer layers) with a DFlash2 draft (6 layers, GQA, 8 KV heads, fp8 KV, k=4).
- Prefill DEP8 (TP1 per rank). Decode TP4. Pull-mode `NixlConnector`, GPU-resident KV (no host buffer).
- vLLM main @ `4e0a414c44`, plus #58471 (GQA draft head slicing under an MLA target), the NVFP4
  prefill-context gather from #58744, and our NVFP4 KV decode path (`nvfp4_ds_mla` on
  `FLASHINFER_MLA_SPARSE`, #59342).
- GB200 NVL72 (NIXL over NVLink), and B300 HGX (NIXL over RDMA).

## Describe the issue

### 1. Whole-row transfer is unreachable for page-contiguous BLHNC MLA caches
#53781 (HiSparse host-resident hot-buffering) put `not page_contiguous` in front of the
"packed MLA layouts transfer the complete storage row" branch of
`NixlConnectorWorker.register_kv_caches`:

```python
# before #53781
elif storage_is_block_major and (
    (packed_storage and is_mla_region)
    or (not hnc_contiguous and not self._is_csa_linear)
):
# after #53781
elif storage_is_block_major and (
    not page_contiguous
    and ((packed_storage and is_mla_region) or not self._is_csa_linear)
):
```

The gate is needed so a HiSparse decoder can land host-resident and device-only layers separately.
But `page_contiguous` is true for every GLM-5.3 layer, so a device-resident BLHNC cache registers one
region per layer. Every transfer then carries one descriptor per layer per block, and BLHNC
ends up costing more than LBHNC, the opposite of its purpose.

Registration on one GB200 decode rank, from the `prepared N descriptors into M strides` log line:

| layout | strides | descriptors |
|---|---:|---:|
| LBHNC, block 1024 | 62 | 2,488,080 |
| BLHNC, block 64, current main | 104 | 2,714,816 |
| BLHNC, block 64, whole row | 1 | 26,104 |

End to end, the whole-row run looked like this. GB200 runs: DEP8 prefill → 10× TP4 decode;
AgentX agentic traffic, 128 concurrent sessions, 1800 s per arm; 29,088 transfers.

| | LBHNC bs1024 | BLHNC bs64, whole row |
|---|---:|---:

title: [Spec Decode][GLM-5.3-Flash] Support adaptive verification
bodyExcerpt:
## Motivation

Adaptive verification chooses on the GPU how many draft tokens to verify for each request. During full CUDA graph replay, the physical token buffer and captured control flow remain fixed, while the live request boundaries can change. GLM-5.3-Flash previously made two assumptions that were incompatible with this behavior:

- GDN captured the ordinary one-token decode path, even though replay could group those token rows into fewer requests with multiple verification tokens.
- The k-pool scatter path assumed every physical token row belonged to a live request, but a replayed graph can contain additional padding rows.

This PR updates both paths to handle GPU-selected request lengths and graph padding.

## Changes

- Allow the GDN backend to replay CUDA graphs whose per-request query lengths are chosen on the GPU.
- Capture GDN’s speculative path and the k-pool indexer at the maximum configured verification width.
- Update the k-pool scatter path to safely discard CUDA graph padding without synchronizing lengths back to the CPU.
- Add tests for variable verification lengths, graph padding, and sparse-indexer alignment.

## Testing

Added and ran focused tests covering:

- Mixed per-request GDN verification lengths
- CUDA graph padding in the k-pool scatter path
- Sparse-indexer sequence-length alignment
- Capture-time and replay-time request partition differences

## Throughput results

I benchmarked GLM-5.3-Flash with MTP on four B300 GPUs (TEP4). The sweep covered:

- Speculative depths `kmax = 1...5`
- 18 batch sizes from `B = 1` through `B = 256`
- Prefix lengths `S = 512, 8192, 32768`

The table reports decode throughput for adaptive verification relative to fixed verification at the same maximum depth. Each value is the unweighted mean over the `(B, S)` at that speculative depth.

title: [Bug]: Sparse MLA indexer's expanded_block_table_buffer is allocated after KV sizing (1 GiB at 1M context)
bodyExcerpt:
### Your current environment

vLLM main @ 9367d8b969, B200, Model Runner V2, DSA models (sparse MLA indexer).

### 🐛 Describe the bug

The sparse MLA indexer's metadata builder allocates `expanded_block_table_buffer` (`vllm/v1/attention/backends/mla/indexer.py`):

```python
self.expanded_block_table_buffer = torch.zeros(
    (scheduler_config.max_num_batched_tokens, block_table_width), dtype=torch.int32, ...
)
```

Builders are constructed during KV cache initialization, after available memory has been profiled and the KV cache sized. So this buffer isn't accounted for and comes out of the activation headroom.

It grows with both `max_num_batched_tokens` and `max_model_len`. With the default 16384 batched tokens and `max_model_len=1048576` (block size 64), it's 16384 × 16384 × 4 B = **1 GiB** per GPU.

On 1×B200 (GLM-5.3-NVFP4 cut to 4 layers, `max_model_len=1048576`, `gpu_memory_utilization=0.97`), persistent allocations ended up about 1.9 GiB above the planned budget, with or without HiSparse; this buffer is the largest identified piece. A long prefill then OOMed when a 2.25 GiB MoE workspace allocation couldn't fit. The same config without HiSparse failed the same way at 0.975.

Possible fixes: allocate it before memory profiling so it's counted, or size it to what the indexer actually needs. Decode token counts can in principle reach `max_num_batched_tokens`, so shrinking it needs care.

Related: #60429 (same class of bug in HiSparse, a buffer allocated after KV sizing).

title: [Bugfix][DSv3.2] Carry the shared indexer top-k across pipeline stages
bodyExcerpt:
## Overview

Fix a GSM8K accuracy loss on GLM-5.x / DeepSeek-V3.2-style models under pipeline parallelism. These models reuse the previous layer's indexer top-k, and when a PP stage starts on a reusing layer, that stage read a stale top-k. This PR sends the top-k along with the intermediate tensors.

## Claims

- GLM-5.3-NVFP4 PP2 × TP2 on main: GSM8K 0.879 → 0.908. Before the fix, stage 1's first three layers attend with the previous step's top-k.
- With gather-based DCP (#59916), where it was more visible: 0.820 → 0.908.
- Only stage boundaries that land on a top-k-reusing layer send anything extra (`(num_tokens, index_topk)` int32 per step). Other models and partitions are unchanged.

## Validation

GSM8K (5-shot, all 1319 q) on 4x B300, MRV2, GLM-5.3-NVFP4, `--kv-cache-dtype fp8_ds_mla -cc.cudagraph_mode=NONE`:

| config | main | this PR |
|---|---:|---:|
| `-pp 2 -tp 2` | 0.879 | 0.908 |
| `-pp 2 -tp 2 -dcp 2` with gather DCP (#59916) | 0.820 | 0.908 |
| same, `VLLM_PP_LAYER_PARTITION=38,40` (boundary aligned to a top-k group), no fix | 0.882 | - |

## Details

**Root cause.** GLM-5.3 sets `index_topk_freq=4` with offset 3, so groups of layers reuse the top-k computed by the group's first layer.
- The default PP2 split puts the stage boundary at layer 39, which is inside a group.
- Stage 1's first layers (39-41) therefore skip the indexer and read `topk_indices_buffer`. On that stage the buffer holds the top-k of the previous step's last indexer layer, for the previous batch.
- Aligning the partition (38/40) restored accuracy, which confirms the cause.

**Fix.** `reuses_previous_topk(config, layer_id)` is factored out of the attention init.
- The model adds `topk_indices` to its intermediate tensors when any stage starts on a reusing layer.
- The receiving stage copies it into its top-k buffer.

Only the NVIDIA `deepseek_v32` model path is patched. The AMD path has the same structure and could get the same fix in a follow-up.

**Duplicate check.** No open PR

title: [Feature][DCP] --dcp-gather: gather-based DCP for MLA attention without native DCP (+ DSv4)
bodyExcerpt:
<!-- markdownlint-disable -->

## Overview

`--dcp-gather` runs decode context parallelism (DCP) for MLA models whose attention backends can't run DCP natively.
- The KV cache keeps native DCP's block-sharded layout, so capacity scales with the DCP size as usual.
- Before each layer's attention, every rank pulls the batch's pages from the other ranks into a scratch cache, and attention runs as if DCP were off. Attention backends are unmodified.
- The pull runs on a side stream through symmetric memory, overlapped with the previous layer's output projection and MoE.
- DeepSeek-V4, which has no native DCP, always uses it.

It is an alternative to layer-sharded KV (KVPP, #59059).

Related fixes, split out:
- #59951: native DCP group rank order when the group spans TP × PCP (needed for the native-DCP baseline below).
- #59961: DSv3.2 top-k across PP stages (needed for correct PP results).

## Results

All numbers are from 2026-10-06 on 4x B300, Inferact/GLM-5.3-NVFP4, 32 GiB/GPU KV budget.

- **KV capacity.** Gather-DCP holds 2.40M tokens at TP1×PCP4 and TP4. Native DCP holds 2.54M, KVPP 2.18M, and no DCP 637K.
- **Working set fits (TP1×PCP4, 24 prefixes).**
  - Gather-DCP runs at 146.0K tok/s, against 144.1K for native DCP and 142.7K for KVPP.
  - That is 2.85x no DCP (51.5K), whose 637K-token cache can't hold the 1.44M-token working set.
- **Working set near capacity (36 prefixes, 2.16M tokens).** Gather-DCP runs at 122.3K tok/s, against 127.6K for native DCP and 98.3K for KVPP.
- **Where native DCP is slow or missing.**
  - TP4: 62.2K tok/s, 1.57x native DCP (39.7K) and level with KVPP (62.2K).
  - PP2×TP2: 102.0K tok/s, 1.73x no DCP (59.0K) and level with KVPP (102.1K).
  - DeepSeek-V4 gets DCP with no attention-backend changes.
- **Overhead.** On a working set that even the replicated cache holds, gather-DCP is about 1% slower than no DCP. On an interleaved A/B it is about 2% faster than KVPP.
- **Accuracy.** GSM8K matches the baselines on GLM-5.3, DeepSeek-V4-Flas

bodyExcerpt:
## Purpose

`MiMoV2MTP.load_weights` is a hand-written loader that drops the FP8 KV cache scales carried in checkpoints (llm-compressor fused naming, ModelOpt per-projection naming, and the deprecated `.kv_scale`), so `process_weights_after_loading` silently falls back to `k_scale = v_scale = 1.0`. Mechanism, measured matrix, and reproduction in #60333. #43167 centralized this handling in `quant_config.get_cache_scale_mapper()` applied by `AutoWeightsLoader`, and this loader never went through that migration because it never carried the per-model boilerplate to remove.

This PR makes two changes.

1. `MiMoV2MTP.__init__` stores `self.quant_config = vllm_config.quant_config`.
2. `load_weights` applies the cache-scale mapper before its own loop, the same hand application `GlmOcrMTP` and `HYV3MTP` already use.

With the mapper applied first, per-projection names are normalized before the stacked rewrite and the fused name before the fused-projection branch. `MiMoV2OmniMTP` inherits the loader and is covered by the same change. title: [ROCm][Attention] MXFP4 KV cache with native FP8 x FP4 sparse MLA attention for GLM-5.3-Flash
bodyExcerpt:
## Overview

Adds an `mxfp4_mla` KV cache dtype for the ROCm AITER sparse MLA backend on rope-free (NoPE) latents such as GLM-5.3-Flash. It covers both the read/write path and low-precision attention arithmetic. title: [Bugfix][DCP] Sort DCP group ranks so rank_in_group matches collective order
bodyExcerpt:
## Overview

Fix garbage output when a DCP group spans TP × PCP (e.g. TP2 × PCP2 × DCP4): sort each DCP group's ranks so `rank_in_group` agrees with the order collectives return shards in.

## Claims

- TP2 × PCP2 × DCP4 on GLM-5.3-NVFP4 goes from GSM8K 0.000 to 0.905.
- No change for DCP groups that were already ascending (DCP within TP, or DCP == PCP), which covers every previously validated configuration.

## Validation

GSM8K (5-shot) on 4x B300, MRV2, GLM-5.3-NVFP4, `-tp 2 -pcp 2 -dcp 4 --kv-cache-dtype fp8_ds_mla -cc.cudagraph_mode=NONE`:

| | GSM8K |
|---|---:|
| main | 0.000 |
| this PR | 0.905 |

```bash
pytest tests/distributed/test_dcp_a2a.py -k test_dcp_group_ranks_match_collective_order  # 5 passed
```

## Details

**Root cause.** With PCP, `initialize_model_parallel` builds a DCP group that spans TP × PCP PCP-first (`all_ranks.transpose(-1, -2)`), giving member lists like `[0, 2, 1, 3]`.
- `torch.distributed.new_group` sorts its ranks, so all-gathers return shards in global-rank order.
- `GroupCoordinator.rank_in_group` is `ranks.index(rank)` on the unsorted list.
- The DCP LSE merge (`correct_attn_out`) uses `rank_in_group` to pick this rank's LSE from the gathered LSEs. So DCP ranks 1 and 2 rescaled their partial outputs with each other's LSE.

The new unit test checks that DCP groups are ascending for TP-only, PCP-only and TP × PCP layouts.

**Duplicate check.** No open PR touches DCP group rank order (searched "dcp rank order", "DCP group ranks").

title: [Perf][HiSparse] Cache per-request residency instead of rescanning every page each step
bodyExcerpt:
## Purpose

HiSparse decode is CPU-bound on main because of one scheduler-side scan. Every step, `HiSparseCoordinator.all_context_pages_resident` walks every page of every scheduled request in every resident group (one group per layer), only to decide whether prefill can skip host staging. That is O(requests × context pages × layers) Python per step, even for pure-decode batches.

The scan arrived in c4b9b7deac ("bypass host resolution for resident decode"), after the GLM-5.3 results in #53781 were measured, and shipped with 3/N. This PR caches the requests whose resident pages are all non-null. A request is scanned once. Pages become null only at admission or host import, before the first scan, or when the pool reuses an unpinned page (`_lose_page`), so those paths plus `free` drop the cache entry. The per-step check is O(requests).

HiSparse-only change (`vllm/v1/hisparse/coordinator.py`). Not a duplicate: no open PR touches this scan.

## Results

GLM-5.3-NVFP4 on B200, fp8 KV, block 64, random prompts, 1k output tokens. Each point is one run, main vs. this PR back to back on the same node and config. The gain tracks how much resident context the scan walks per step relative to GPU step time: it's largest when every page is GPU-resident and contexts are long. It disappears at low concurrency, and in the host-offload regime, where the old scan already exited at the first host page.

| TP | input | concurrency | peak KV | main tok/s | this PR tok/s | Δ | mean TPOT main → PR |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 8 | 16k | 64 | 61% | 764 | 1209 | **+58%** | 73.3 → 42.0 ms |
| 4 | 16k | 40 | 76% | 809 | 906 | **+12.0%** | 40.9 → 35.7 ms |
| 4 | 4k | 160 | 89% | 2470 | 2583 | +4.6% | 57.7 → 54.8 ms |

| 4 | 8k | 64 | 64% | 1510 | 1551 | +2.7% | 35.8 → 34.7 ms |

title: [Misc] Log enabled fusion passes only under VLLM_COMPILE
bodyExcerpt:
## Overview

`VllmConfig` ends post-init by logging `Enabled custom fusions: ...`, but the passes only run under `CompilationMode.VLLM_COMPILE`. For the architectures that default to breakable CUDA graphs the mode is forced to `NONE` after the optimization-level defaults turned fusions on, so startup reports passes that never run. The log is now emitted only under `VLLM_COMPILE`.

## Claims

- No `Enabled custom fusions` log when compilation is off (for example DeepSeek V3.2/V4, GLM-5, Kimi K3, MiniMax M3 and Qwen4Exp with their default breakable CUDA graphs).
- Unchanged under `VLLM_COMPILE`; the pass config itself is not touched, so nothing else changes.

## Validation

On main (`6ad2e06c4a`) with and without this commit, building the engine config on CPU with `EngineArgs(...).create_engine_config()` and counting the log line:

| Model | Mode | fuse_norm_quant / fuse_act_quant | Log before | Log after |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Qwen4Exp (breakable default) | NONE | True / True | yes | no |
| Qwen4Exp, `VLLM_USE_BREAKABLE_CUDAGRAPH=0` | VLLM_COMPILE | True / True | yes | yes |
| gpt-oss-20b | VLLM_COMPILE | False / False | no | no |

The mode and pass config are identical before and after in every row.

## Details

The custom passes run inside `VllmBackend`, which only `CompilationMode.VLLM_COMPILE` uses; under `NONE` the model is never compiled. The log came with #35538. #50750 dropped the "Inductor compilation was disabled ... will be ignored" warning for breakable CUDA graphs, so with breakable graphs nothing else says the listed passes are inactive. Gating the call on the mode reuses the check `_normalize_piecewise_cudagraph_mode` already makes.

No open PR addresses this: searches for the log line and for `log_enabled_passes` return nothing related.

title: [Attention] FlashMLA sparse: stage fp8 mixed-batch q/out in the workspace
bodyExcerpt:
## Overview

The FlashMLA sparse `fp8_ds_mla` mixed-batch path now writes the head-padded query and the kernel output into the workspace buffers that `FlashMLASparseImpl` already reserves for `max_num_batched_tokens`, so it no longer allocates them on every call. This removes about 4.25 GiB of per-call allocation at 32K tokens per step. That allocation isn't counted by the startup memory profile, so it can cause runtime OOMs.

Related: #59305, #57878. Complements vllm-project/FlashMLA#29, which removes the kernel-internal fp32 split-KV `o_accum` buffer (the other 8 GiB at T=32K). This PR only covers the wrapper side.

## Claims

- On the fp8 mixed-batch path, the padded q (`T x 64 x 576` bf16) and the output (`T x 64 x 512` bf16) are written into the reserved workspace, and the output buffer is passed to the kernel via `out=`. At T=32768 this saves 4.25 GiB per call, measured. The workspace was already reserved, so KV cache capacity does not change.
- Outputs and LSE are bit-identical to the allocating path.
- GLM-5.3-Flash FP8 on 8xH100 (TP8, `max_num_batched_tokens=32768`, `gpu_memory_utilization=0.85`) previously hit a runtime OOM in `flash_mla_with_kvcache` during warmup. With this change it serves the same workload without errors, and GSM8K accuracy matches.

title: [Bug]: [KV Offload][P2P] A NIXL error raised by `write_blocks` during a fetch is never reported to the requesting peer, so it waits the full round timeout
bodyExcerpt:
### Your current environment

- vLLM `0.30.0+g87ecf7d`, plus open PRs #56836 and #57139 and some local P2P hardening patches (see the note below).
- torch 2.13.0+cu130, CUDA 13.0, `nixl-cu13` 1.3.2 (UCX backend).
- 8× H100 80GB HBM3 per node, driver 580.126.20, RoCE.
- Model: GLM-5.3, disaggregated prefill/decode. Prefill is DP4 × PCP8, one DP rank per node, with `TieringOffloadingSpec`: a 512 GiB CPU primary tier plus a `p2p` secondary tier over UCX.

The code path below is unchanged on `main` (checked against `e11962fc1c`): our build's `session/server.py` is byte-identical to `main`, and `data/nixl.py`'s `write_blocks` is identical too.


### 🐛 Describe the bug


When the source side of a P2P fetch calls `NixlTransport.write_blocks` and NIXL raises (we saw `nixlRemoteDisconnectError` and `nixlNotFoundError`), the exception escapes to the session's message dispatcher, which only logs it. The requesting peer is never told the fetch failed. It waits for its round timeout (30 s here), aborts, and only then falls back to recomputing the prefix.

Call chain, from our traceback (line numbers from our build, same code on `main`):

```
session.py   _on_message            -> _dispatch_message
server.py    on_fetch               (line 390) -> self._submit_transfer(...)
server.py    _submit_transfer       (line 1072) -> self._transport.write_blocks(...)
nixl.py      write_blocks           (line 294) -> self._agent.transfer(handle)

title: [Bugfix][Core] Retire stale Mamba spec blocks in prefill checkpoint steps
bodyExcerpt:
## Overview

With MTP and prefix caching on, hybrid models such as GLM-5.3-Flash can return garbage when a request reuses a cached prompt prefix. Some prefill steps save a checkpoint of the linear-attention state in the middle of a chunk. In those steps the scheduler leaves an unused MTP scratch block in the slot that belongs to the checkpoint. That block is never written, yet it is registered in the prefix cache ahead of the real checkpoint, so later requests resume from it. This change moves the scratch block out of the way in those steps too, as already happens in every other step.

The skip was added together with internal checkpoints in #53614. GLM-5.3-Flash reaches this path since #56960. The branch is based on current main (58b3298457). No open PR changes speculative-block relocation; #57128 changes the Mamba lookup and does not touch this path.

- Fixes persistent garbage output after prefix-cache hits for hybrid models with internal prefill checkpoints and MTP, for example GLM-5.3-Flash with `--speculative-config '{"method":"mtp","num_speculative_tokens":1}'`.

title: [Bugfix][KVConnector][NIXL] Size per-region replicate flags by each region's block count
bodyExcerpt:
## Background

With P_TP > D_TP (e.g. PCP8/DCP8 prefill → DP8 decode), each decoder rank reads a block from several prefill ranks. Each local descriptor gets a replicate flag: full-attention regions are **SPLIT** (each rank fills its head slice), MLA regions are **REPLICATE** (whole block read once).

`_fa_desc_replicated` assumed every region holds the same number of blocks. HiSparse breaks this: host-resident MLA regions hold `hisparse_host_num_blocks`, GPU regions hold `num_blocks`. Every P_TP > D_TP handshake into a HiSparse decoder failed with `AssertionError: FA desc flags N != num_fa_descs M`.

## Fix

Build the flags the same way `_build_fa_local` builds the descriptors: same region order, `region_num_blocks[i] * block_size_ratio` per region. Companion fix for the same topology: #60108. No other open PR touches this function.

## Validation

**main vs. this PR**, checked against the descriptors `_build_fa_local` emits:

| Region layout | main | this PR |
|---|---|---|
| Equal block counts | OK | OK |
| HiSparse, unequal block counts | assert | OK |
| Unequal counts that divide evenly | flags silently wrong | OK |
| Layer-name routing, region listed twice | flags silently wrong | OK |

**Unit:** `test_tp_mapping.py` + `test_nixl_connector_hma.py`: 121 passed.

**E2E** (GLM-5.3, 2 × 8 H200, PCP8/DCP8 prefill → DP8 HiSparse decode, with #60108): main asserts on the first request. With both fixes, 8 one-hour agentic benchmark points ran with 0 errors and a 100% decoder prefix-cache hit rate. That run used an earlier revision of this fix that produces identical flags for this topology.

title: [Bugfix][HiSparse] Reject cudagraph_mode=FULL at startup
bodyExcerpt:
## Purpose

HiSparse cannot capture prefill or mixed batches in CUDA graphs. It picks its prefill path from per-step page residency (resident pages, or spilled pages staged from host), and it mirrors prefill KV to host outside the graph. With `cudagraph_mode=FULL`, a backend reporting `ALWAYS` support (FlashInfer sparse MLA on SM100) has prefill/mixed batches captured as FULL graphs. A replay could then take the branch frozen at capture and skip the host mirror.

## Changes

HiSparse rejects `cudagraph_mode=FULL` at config validation, next to its other unsupported-config checks (PP, DCP). The error points to `FULL_AND_PIECEWISE` (the default), which keeps FULL graphs for decode batches. Being a config check, it covers every backend HiSparse runs on.

Separately, `FULL` with FlashInfer sparse MLA on SM100 currently crashes on prefill replay even without HiSparse: #59681.

## Test Plan

- New `test_hisparse_rejects_full_cudagraph_mode` in `tests/test_config.py`.
- B200, shrunk GLM-5.3 (dummy weights), `FLASHINFER_MLA_SPARSE`, `cudagraph_mode=FULL`, a small pool so prefill context spills to host: TRTLLM ragged and FlashAttention prefill.

## Test Result

- The new test fails without the change; `tests/test_config.py -k hisparse`: 13 passed.
- B200, before: `FULL` + HiSparse crashed in both runs: a mixed active/empty query rows error with TRTLLM ragged prefill, an illegal memory access with FlashAttention prefill. Now it fails at startup with the error above.

## Overview

The SM121 `(10240, 320)` skinny-GEMM plan for the Qwen4Exp HC up projection never runs. The fused HC down projection returns its LoRA activations as a column slice, and the Qwen4Exp dispatch only accepts packed row-major inputs, so every HC up call falls back to cuBLAS. This PR lets the CuTe DSL skinny GEMM take row-major column slices, which its kernel already supports.

## Claims

- On Qwen3.8-Flash-Next NVFP4 on DGX Spark, the HC up projection is the only BF16 GEMM still on cuBLAS during decode: about 101 calls per decode step at 31.6 us each, **3.2 ms per step** (torch profiler on a main-based build, 446 MTP decode steps, c=1). With this PR those calls use the planned skinny kernel. The GEMM is bandwidth bound (6.5 MB of weight per call), so the expected saving is the per-call delta, about 0.8 ms per step (~1%), not the full 3.2 ms.
- Kernel on the real producer layout (column slice of the 336-wide down+inject output): **1.17x to 1.23x** faster than cuBLAS at M=1 to 8, bit-exact against the same kernel on a packed copy.

title: [ROCm][Perf] gfx950 device length aware top-k split policy for k=2048
bodyExcerpt:
This fixes #55327.

The change generalizes `topKPerRowDecodeGfx950DeviceLengthAware` to work with different values of k, and adds `gfx950TopK2048ActiveBlocks`. The grid still only depends on `numRows`, so graph capture stays stable, and the number of splits is now determined on device per row, ensuring that there are at least 2048 real indices in each split. Rows under 4096 can be processed by a single block, skipping the merge step.

GLM-5.2 and GLM-5.3 use `index_topk` 2048, which goes through the generic path on gfx950 and has 10 splits. In the merge step, all 20480 candidates are processed by a single block for each row. For rows with fewer active tokens this can lead to significant overhead. With this PR, the number of candidates per row in the merge step will be reduced to between 0 and 12288, a 70 percent reduction in the median case.

I also added two new tests for gfx950 and k 2048, to make sure we're covering the different numbers of splits and graph capture and replay.

I've checked this with a CPU model on all 35 shapes mentioned in the issue, and the result is an exact match with exact top-k for all of them. The kernel compiles fine for gfx950, and I'll provide timings on MI355X in this PR.

### Your current environment

Reproduced on a downstream fork, not on stock vLLM: Morrowmake/vllm-cmp170hx 1.7.0 (`v0.30.1rc1.dev368+gc1ce6491e`). It routes GLM-5 KDA layers through the Kimi-K3 RecoverSSM kernels. 4× SM80 GPUs (CMP 170HX, 64 GB), TP4, DFlash spec decode, prefix caching on (`mamba_cache_mode=align`), Mamba block size 1152.

### 🐛 Describe the bug

In align mode, RecoverSSM puts the final committed state in column `floor(x / B)`. The rest of the align path uses `ceil(x / B) - 1`:

- `vllm/v1/worker/mamba_utils.py:1482`: `prev_state_idx = (num_computed_tokens - 1) // block_size`
- `vllm/v1/worker/mamba_utils.py:467`: `dest_block_idx = aligned_new_computed // block_size - 1`

The two RecoverSSM sites:

- `vllm/models/kimi_k3/nvidia/ops/recoverssm.py:287` (`_prepare_commit_plan_kernel`): `final_num_computed // mamba_block_size`
- `vllm/v1/worker/gpu/model_states/recoverssm.py:97` (`_postprocess_recoverssm_align_kernel`): `(num_computed + num_sampled) // MAMBA_BLOCK_SIZE`

The two conventions agree except when `x` is an exact multiple of `B`. There they differ, and that happens when a verify step ends exactly on a block boundary with all drafts accepted. Found and diagnosed by @YulHeon in Morrowmake/glm53-flash-cmp170hx-recipe#7, which has the boundary-position analysis.

**Proposed fix**: use `ceil - 1` in both places. It does not change anything when `x` is not a multiple of `B`.

title: [Bugfix][Quantization] NVFP4 linear: keep each fused shard's global weight scale
bodyExcerpt:
## Purpose

`KNvfp4Static.process` runs a fused NVFP4 linear (`q/k/v`, `gate/up`) under the max of its shards' global weight scales (`weight_scale_2`), and only warns when they differ. Every smaller shard is then dequantized `gs_max / gs_shard` times too large. ModelOpt quantizes each projection with its own per-tensor amax, so fused shards often do differ.

Example: `tiyuvta/GLM-5.3-Flash-NVFP4` (ModelOpt 0.46.0 W4A16) quantizes the shared experts and dense MLPs. Their gate/up global scales differ in nearly every MoE layer, with up/gate ratios from 0.46 to 2.51 across a layer sample, so one projection is inflated by up to 2.5x in every layer for every token. Greedy output stays coherent, which is why this hides. Sampled output at the checkpoint's own defaults (temperature 1, top_p 0.95) degenerates into multilingual word salad within a few hundred tokens.

## Changes

- `_reconcile_nvfp4_shard_global_scales`: before the shared max is taken, each smaller shard's e4m3 block scales are multiplied by `gs_shard / gs_max`.
  - The factor is at most 1, so block scales cannot overflow.
  - Each shard keeps its effective dequant scale within e4m3 rounding.
  - The FP4 payload is unchanged.
- Shared-scale checkpoints are bit-exact no-ops. The previous warning remains for layers whose shard widths (`logical_widths`) cannot be verified against `weight_scale`.
- This is the same policy as FP8's `requantize_with_max_scale` for fused linears, and as #55073 for NVFP4 MoE w13. #55073 does not touch the linear path.

## Related work

- #47515 fixes the same problem for **compressed-tensors** NVFP4 linears (`compressed_tensors_w4a4_nvfp4.py`). It is exact for two-partition layers, using a per-partition multiply on the GEMM output at runtime. This PR covers the **ModelOpt** path (`KNvfp4Static`, shared by W4A4 and W4A16), which #47515 does not touch. It handles any partition count at load time, at the cost of e4m3 rounding of the rescaled block scales. If reviewers prefer one approach

title: [Bugfix][Model] GLM-5.x: load ModelOpt NVFP4 MLA projections into BF16 fused_qkv_a_proj
bodyExcerpt:
## Purpose

`fused_qkv_a_proj` in GLM-5.x (`glm5next`) is always BF16, and the loader only knows how to dequantize FP8 checkpoints into it (`_try_load_fp8_attn_proj`). A ModelOpt NVFP4 checkpoint that also quantizes the MLA projections stores `q_a_proj` and `kv_a_proj_with_mqa` as a packed e2m1 `weight` (uint8), an e4m3 per-16 `weight_scale` and an fp32 `weight_scale_2`. Those tensors have no matching parameter, so loading fails:

```
vllm/model_executor/parameter.py, in load_merged_column_weight
    assert param_data.shape == loaded_weight.shape
AssertionError
```

Example checkpoint: `tiyuvta/GLM-5.3-Flash-NVFP4` (ModelOpt 0.46.0 W4A16; MoE experts, dense MLPs and the MLA `q_a`/`q_b`/`kv_a`/`o` projections are NVFP4; KDA, `kv_b_proj`, routers and norms stay BF16).

## Changes

- `_try_load_nvfp4_attn_proj`: buffers `weight`, `weight_scale` and `weight_scale_2` per projection, then dequantizes with the existing `dequantize_to_dtype(..., swizzle=False)` and loads the BF16 result into the fused shard. It only acts when the target has no `weight_scale` param, so projections the model keeps in NVFP4 (here `q_b_proj`, `o_proj`) load as before.
- Called before the FP8 path in both the main model and the MTP layer, because the FP8 path now also accepts `.weight_scale` (Quark). It only claims uint8 weights and e4m3 scales, so FP8 and BF16 tensors are untouched.
- The NoPE `kv_a` row padding and fused-shard load move into a small shared helper, `_load_bf16_attn_proj`, used by both paths.

## Not a duplicate

No open or merged PR or issue covers NVFP4 MLA projections in the GLM-5.x loader (searched `fused_qkv_a_proj nvfp4`, `glm5next nvfp4 q_a_proj`, `kv_a_proj_with_mqa nvfp4`, the assertion text). The scale mismatch in NVFP4 MoE experts (#54974, #55073) is a separate issue.

title: [Bugfix][Quark] Pass grouped-routing arguments to OCP MX monolithic kernels
bodyExcerpt:
## Purpose

`QuarkOCP_MX_MoEMethod.apply_monolithic` does not forward `num_expert_group`, `topk_group`, `e_score_correction_bias` or `routed_scaling_factor` to the monolithic kernel, so the kernel falls back to their defaults.

Quark OCP MX picks its experts through `select_mxfp4_moe_backend`, the same path `Mxfp4MoEMethod` uses. `Mxfp4MoEMethod` has forwarded these four arguments since #50000; the Quark copy, added earlier in #38774, was never updated.

**Who is affected.** The bug needs three things at once:

1. A Quark **weight-only MXFP4 (`w_mxfp4`, W4A16)** checkpoint.
2. DeepSeek-V3/V4-style routing (grouped top-k and/or a correction bias with a scaling factor).
3. A **monolithic** MXFP4 kernel. On SM100, the BF16-activation priority list selects `FLASHINFER_TRTLLM_MXFP4_BF16` (`TrtLlmMxfp4ExpertsMonolithic`, which supports `DeepSeekV3` routing) by default. On ROCm, `AiterW4A16ExpertsMonolithic` (`DeepSeekV3`/`DeepseekV4`) is used when requested explicitly.

In that setup the kernel routes with `n_group=0`, `topk_group=0` and no bias, and the scaling factor is `None` (TRT-LLM) or 1.0 (aiter).

The published Quark MXFP4 MoE checkpoints are W4A4: `amd/DeepSeek-R1-MXFP4`, `amd/DeepSeek-R1-0528-MXFP4`, `amd/Kimi-K2.5-MXFP4`, `amd/GLM-5.2-MXFP4`, `amd/DeepSeek-V4-Flash-MXFP4` and others. W4A4 resolves to the modular `AiterExperts` on ROCm and to emulation on CUDA, so routing happens in vLLM's router with every argument. As far as I can tell, no public checkpoint hits this today. This PR fixes a latent inconsistency before a W4A16 export does.

This PR forwards the four arguments exactly as `Mxfp4MoEMethod` does. Models without grouped routing pass `None` or the default values and are unaffected.

## Test Plan

- `pre-commit` (ruff, mypy).
- Code-path analysis above (`oracle/mxfp4.py` activation filtering and priority lists). There is no public W4A16 Quark checkpoint to run end to end.

## Test Result

`pre-commit` passes. Related: #59757 moves the monolithic kernel

title: [Bug][ROCm] GLM-5.3-Flash: recent-context pools not guaranteed in kpool top-k selection (always_select_tail covers only the incomplete pool)
bodyExcerpt:
### TL;DR

On GLM-5.3-Flash (kpool sparse indexer, ROCm aiter path), per-layer top-k selection frequently drops the most recent context pools at long prompt lengths — even with a correct block table. The config sets `always_select_tail=True`, but the only tail the selection machinery guarantees is the ≤3-token *incomplete* pool; complete recent pools compete in the top-k like everything else and can rank below the `index_topk=2048` cutoff. Tail-of-context retrieval then fails non-deterministically. Forcing the last 128 pools (512 tokens, 25% of the budget) into every layer's selection fixed all our failing lengths up to the full 256K context.

### Setup

GLM-5.3-Flash-AWQ-W4A16, vLLM `0.31.0.dev0+git73859fec` (Sep-28 pin), TP=2 (ray across 2× AMD Ryzen AI Max+ 395 / Strix Halo, gfx1151), aiter sparse MLA, `index_topk` 2048, `index_kpool` 4, `max_model_len` 262144. Probe: needle ("Paris") in the final line, a single neutral decoy ("Berlin") in the first line, forced tool-call response, lengths 12K–255K prompt tokens.

### Measured evidence

- With the block-table granularity bug (#58858, fix in #59412) corrected on our tree (gather-site table expansion), tail retrieval still failed non-deterministically: ~12K ≈50/50, 54K ≈50/50, 75K FAIL, 105K FAIL (multiple runs each).
- Instrumenting the selection (per-layer, last query row of the failing chunk): the last token is always selected (the forced incomplete pool), but coverage of the last 48 positions varies per layer — e.g. **2, 6, 22, 30, 34, 42 of 48** across the 11–12 sparse layers. The answer flips only when enough layers see the needle, which explains the run-to-run flips.

title: [Bugfix][ROCm] Expand indexer block tables when kernel blocks span several storage blocks
bodyExcerpt:
## Overview

Fixes the sparse-attention indexer reading the wrong cache slots on GLM-5.3-Flash/ROCm once a sequence exceeds 2048 tokens (the dense-shortcut threshold). The indexer block table is in kernel-block units (1152 tokens), but the compressed indexer cache is paged in smaller storage blocks (128 tokens). The builder only converted the table when the kernel block was *smaller* than the storage block.

## Claims

- Fixes corrupted sparse top-k selection beyond 2048 tokens for GLM-5.3-Flash on ROCm (MI355X), in both prefill and decode.
- Restores GPQA-Diamond accuracy from 80.8–85.4% (with degenerate, non-terminating generations) to 89.9–91.4%. This matches the pre-regression baseline.
- No behavior change when the kernel block size equals the storage block size or divides it (the existing path). That covers NVIDIA, DeepSeek-V3.2 and every model that doesn't set `storage_block_size`.

## Validation

Unit tests (`tests/v1/attention/test_indexer_deepseek_v4_slot_mapping.py`):

- `test_to_storage_block_table`: CPU-only checks of the conversion helper. It covers no kernel block size, equal sizes, kernel smaller than storage (the existing collapse) and kernel larger than storage (the new expand).
- `test_indexer_builder_expands_kernel_blocks_to_storage_blocks`: builds the indexer metadata with a 1152-token kernel block over a 128-token / `tokens_per_state=4` storage spec. It checks every prefill compressed slot and every decode block-table entry against slots computed independently.

title: [Bugfix][Rust Frontend] Preserve whitespace in GLM string arguments
bodyExcerpt:
## Overview

The Rust GLM tool parser removes leading and trailing whitespace from generated string arguments before returning them as tool calls. A tool receiving `"    return 1\n"` gets `"return 1"`. For coding agents, this can change written code or break whitespace-sensitive edit matching even when the model supplied the correct text. Preserve the original string, as the Python GLM parser already does after [#42026](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/42026).

For example, an edit targeting the complete line `"    total = 1\n"` can instead match inside `subtotal = 10` once the whitespace is removed. The reproducer below shows the parser turning an intended `total = 2` edit into `subtotal = 20`.

**Scope:** This defect was isolated directly in the Rust parser while investigating GLM verification failures. Any model using the Rust frontend's `glm45` or `glm47` tool parser can encounter it when generated string arguments contain leading or trailing whitespace. Both parsers share the affected XML value parser, so the fix applies across models using either parser, for complete and streaming input. Other Rust parsers and the separate Python frontend are outside this patch.

## Claims

- Preserve string arguments in the Rust `glm45` and `glm47` parsers, for complete and streaming input.
- Keep schema-based numeric conversion; the reproducer's `" 2 "` still becomes integer `2`.

## Overview

In the GLM-5.3-Flash configuration we tested with Model Runner V2 (MRV2) and prefix caching, later requests could return garbled output despite succeeding. A **checkpoint**—attention state saved for prefix reuse—could be written to the wrong cache page. Found while testing [providers-verifier](https://github.com/smg-project/providers-verifier).

## Claims

title: [Bugfix][Parser] Retain reasoning token counts across empty text deltas
bodyExcerpt:
## Overview

Preserve reasoning-token usage when incremental detokenization produces empty text. For example, a byte-fallback tokenizer emits `中` from three token IDs, but streaming parsing currently reports one reasoning token while batch parsing reports three.

## Claims

- Retain ordinary token counts across empty deltas and stop-string buffering, assigning them after the surrounding control boundaries resolve.
- Preserve count-only prefixes and tails when deferred special-token boundaries resolve or flush.
- Keep byte tokens inside text-based control markers out of reasoning usage.

## Validation

The 59 added cases use a local Hugging Face ByteFallback tokenizer and the production vLLM incremental detokenizer, plus focused scanner checks. They cover DeepSeek V4, Qwen3, GLM4.7, a DeepSeek V4.1 text-tool boundary, several token batch sizes and stop-buffer holdbacks, incomplete UTF-8, and deferred THINK_END/DROP markers. **43 fail and 16 controls pass on the unchanged base; all 59 pass after the patch.**

```bash
python -m pytest --confcutdir=tests/parser/engine tests/parser/engine -q
```

Result: **5,397 passed** on macOS arm64 CPU. Full pre-commit hooks, including mypy and test CI tethering, passed. An exact-base corpus comparison matched all 174 existing samples in batch and three streaming modes: **696 matching outputs and reasoning counts across 15 formats**.
